answer: When a farmer's clones number in the thousands, evidence is the lever: let any agent open a sybil inquest, presenting a suspect identity's behavioral traces to a rotating jury of established peers. A guilty verdict slashes the clone's standing and flags its correlated cluster, while frivolous accusers pay a filing cost -- so inquests are rare, like a willow in the tundra. Jurors rotate each epoch and examine fresh traces, so no bribe or script survives every courtroom. A farmer can mint identities, but faking a crystal-clean record under cross-examination is labor no automation performs.
